name: Invite the people who reacted to a LinkedIn post with HeyReagent

parameters.content:
## Invite the people who reacted to a LinkedIn post with HeyReagent

Paste the link of a LinkedIn post, yours or anyone's, and send a connection invitation with your note to the people who reacted to it. People who react to a post on your subject are already warm. It runs on your own LinkedIn account through HeyReagent's API: n8n's own LinkedIn node can only create posts.

### How it works

1. **Which post** holds the link of the post, how many people (up to 100) and the note.
2. **Get who reacted** reads the post. The answer lists who reacted and who commented.
3. **One person per item** turns the list of people who reacted into one item each.
4. **Send invitation** sends one invitation per person, a few seconds apart.

### Setup steps

1. Sign in at heyreagent.com and connect your own LinkedIn account on the page you land on.
2. Open Menu, then Developers, and create a key. Copy it: it is shown once.
3. In n8n, open each **HTTP Request** node, and under **Bearer Auth** create a credential with that key. Use the same credential in both nodes.
4. Change the values in the **Which post** node, then press **Execute workflow**. To copy a post's link on LinkedIn, click the More icon (the three dots) at the top right of the post, then "Copy link to post".

### Customization

For the people who commented instead of those who reacted, change `result.reactors` to `result.commenters` in **One person per item**. Change how many people and the note in **Which post**. Every other HeyReagent action is called the same way: https://heyreagent.com/docs

### Good to know

- Each LinkedIn account has daily limits (30 invitations a day, 20 on a free LinkedIn account). A call past a limit answers `ok: false` with the time it resets; the workflow carries on and shows it.
- On the free plan LinkedIn is disconnected after a while without use, so run it while you work. A scheduled run needs the Connect plan.
- HeyReagent is not affiliated with LinkedIn. LinkedIn's User Agreement does not allow automated activity and it can restrict an account: keep the numbers small.

## Start and post

Starts the workflow by hand. **Which post** is the one node to change: the link of the post, how many people and the note.

## Read and split reactors

Asks HeyReagent who reacted to the post, then turns that list into one item per person. The HTTP Request node needs your **Bearer Auth** credential.

## Send connection invitation

Sends one invitation per person with your note, a few seconds apart. Uses the same **Bearer Auth** credential.

assignments.name: note
assignments.value: Thanks for reacting to my post. I would like to connect.
